transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-19 14:00 PT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Nina (CSM), Liam (HeliosPay Head of ML), Sara (VP Product), Diego (SRE), Mei (Finance)
Shared: QBR deck (https://redwood.ai/qbr/heliospay-deck), cost spreadsheet link noted in chat

Summary:
Top themes: rising inference costs during peak checkout flows, two outage blips in October, interest in reserved capacity or hybrid (dedicated for peak, hosted for baseline), security/compliance checklist alignment, decision timeline for pilot in December.

[00:00] Jordan: okay, hey everyone thanks for carving out time for the QBR, I think we'll run through usage trends, incidents, and then map to cost levers and next steps. Does that sound good?
[00:22] Sara: yep that works, and we have Mei here to talk budgeting constraints too.
[00:30] Liam: quick note, our traffic spike in mid-Oct is the thing we want to make sure is addressed in any proposal.
[00:42] Priya: got it, we'll surface latency & tail percentiles and also the aborted requests rate.

[01:15] Diego: just to set context, we run inference for fraud-decisions and checkout recommendations, 1 primary region, occasional cross-region fallbacks, current monthly tokens ~ 420M but cost spikey month-to-month.
[01:40] Mei: from finance, predictable unit cost matters for the Kaizen budget — we can't have surprise 2x months.

[02:05] Jordan: quick slide, here's the usage chart — steady baseline with 3 big spikes. Note: one spike aligned with marketing drop and one with a DB failover where retries amplified requests.
[02:38] Liam: yeah one of those was our issue, but the other looked like increased model temperature iterations. transcribed badly, but essentially dev team A was experimenting and, uh, sending more tokens.

[05:10] Priya: we ran the recent telemetry — p95 latency at baseline is 120ms, p99 at 760ms during spikes. There's also higher KV cache misses when sequence lengths vary. That increases cost because batching breaks down.
[05:45] Diego: the 760 look is what caused two of our checkout timeouts — users got an error.

[07:00] Jordan: tradeoffs: hosted mode gives you quick scaling but variable cost; dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower per-token price but commit is required. Hybrid lets you keep hosted for overflow.
[07:34] Sara: we're interested in hybrid, but we need hard numbers — how much committed cap to recommend for our traffic shape?

[09:00] Priya: we'll recommend a sizing range based on p95 requests and tails. For HeliosPay, an initial dedicated pool covering 60-70% of peak QPS reduces burst cost by ~35% in our model, plus autoscale for the rest. We'll validate with sample traffic.

[11:12] Mei: finance question — what is the minimum term? We need quarterly commitments to match forecasting, not annual if possible.
[11:30] Jordan: we can offer a 3-month pilot reserved capacity — it's often used as a bridge to a 12-month commit once reliability gains are proven.

[13:00] Liam: security review — we run PCI-adjacent flows, we need KMS integration for key management, audit logs for every inference request, and SSO for role-based access. Do you have SOC2?
[13:25] Nina: yes, Redwood is SOC2 Type II, we have a compliance pack. We also support customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS and HSM integrations in our Private deployment. I'll share the docs.
[13:58] Diego: can we get the log retention policy details — we can't retain PII and need redaction in logs.
[14:20] Priya: logs can be configured: token-level logs are optional, we support redaction and policy-based retention, we also have per-request metadata only option. We'll surface a config matrix.

[16:50] Sara: on performance — what's the expected latency improvement if we move 70% of traffic to dedicated?
[17:05] Priya: typical p99 improvements of 20-40% due to steady batch formation and less cold-start. For HeliosPay's pattern we expect p99 from ~760ms down to ~480ms in many cases, but we'll validate.

[18:40] Jordan: pricing note — reserved capacity reduces per-token cost but you pay for reserved GPU hours. The net impact depends on utilization. That's where the cost spreadsheet helps.
[19:10] Mei: can you model 60%, 75%, 90% utilization scenarios?
[19:22] Jordan: yes, and we'll include burst/overflow cost assumptions.

[21:50] Liam: any concerns about model variant fallbacks? We do reranking for risk, so quality regressions are sensitive.
[22:10] Priya: Redwood supports rollout policies and we can pin model versions and run canary comparisons; there's also quality monitoring tied to prompt sets. We'll configure alerts if score deltas > threshold.

[25:00] Diego: about private deployment — we might consider Private (VPC) for our most sensitive tokens, but that adds ops overhead. Could you summarize the differences?
[25:30] Jordan: sure — Private gives customer-managed network, KMS integration, and on-prem options. Hosted is easiest to start. Dedicated is a reserved capacity model that can be hosted or private depending on contract.

[27:40] Sara: timeline — we want to decide on pilot by mid-December so engineering can allocate resources. Is that feasible?
[28:00] Jordan: yes, schedule a 2-week pilot start window in early December; we'll need prompt sets, traffic replay plan, and SSO/KMS details.

[29:15] Priya: technical note on benchmarks — we'll need a 24-hour traffic replay at real traffic variance to capture batching behavior; synthetic p99 tail tests don't capture mixed sequence lengths.
[29:45] Liam: we'll prepare anonymized traffic and a replay harness.

[32:10] Nina: meeting notes — action items: pricing, security pack, bench run, file sharing.

[33:05] Diego: one more operational ask — can you provide runbooks for fallback behavior when a model variant degrades? We want automatic fallback to the last-known-good model.
[33:30] Priya: yes we have automated fallback policies and model-compatibility checks; I'll include the runbook excerpt.

[36:00] Mei: on billing — do you have token-level invoices and daily spend alerts?
[36:18] Jordan: yes daily cost dashboards and token-level breakouts are available; we can also set thresholds to trigger slack/email alerts.

[38:10] Liam: any performance tradeoff with quantized models? We sometimes need exactness for risk scoring.
[38:30] Priya: quantization can reduce latency/cost but risks small quality delta; for risk scoring we recommend mixed strategy: unquantized model for critical paths, quantized for low-risk features. We'll show prior delta examples.

[41:00] Sara: competitor note — we've talked to CloudEndpointX who offered a lower headline price but no strong observability.
[41:20] Jordan: that's a common tradeoff — we emphasize observability + rollouts which reduces production incidents.

[44:00] Priya: I'll run the bench with your replay, include cost breakdown by token, avg batch size, p95/p99 latencies and KV miss rate.

[46:10] Liam: one sticky point: can you support per-customer RBAC inside our org with SAML groups?
[46:28] Nina: yes - SAML/SSO and role sync are supported, we map groups to roles in the console and can limit model access by role.

[48:00] Jordan: recap - Redwood to send: reserved pricing + scenario models, security and KMS docs, Priya's benchmark, and then schedule follow-up to choose pilot size. HeliosPay to send anonymized prompt set and replay logs.

[49:10] Sara: thanks — if we get the bench numbers and a 3-month pilot that shows reliability we'll likely move forward.
[49:30] Mei: finance will review the pilot economics once we get the spreadsheet.

[52:00] Jordan: agreed — we'll aim to deliver docs by end of next week and lock down a Dec pilot. Anything else?
[52:12] Diego: can you include an appendix on how KV cache sizing affects cost? That was helpful in the deck.
[52:30] Priya: yes, adding KV cache sizing and a short primer on batch tuning.

[54:00] Jordan: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the notes and drop calendar for the follow-up.
[54:15] Sara: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
